questions.stem: Which of the following fatty acid present in fish oil is known for its cardio-protective function?
questions.solutionHtml:
Eicosapentaenoic acid

Eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA):

  • ω3 fatty acid
  • Present in fish-oil
  • Known for its cardio-protective action
  • EPA inhibits the formation of thromboxanes (TX2) which are potent platelet aggregators.
  • Hence, the intake of ω3 fatty acids promotes platelet disaggregation.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 207

questions.stem: Phospholipases are hydrolases that act on phospholipids to release fatty acids and are important mediators of signal transduction pathways. Snake venom contains which of the following phospholipases?
questions.solutionHtml:
Phospholipase A2
  • Snake venom
    • Contains Phospholipase A2 (PLA2)
    • PLA 2 hydrolyzes the ester bond at position 2 of phospholipids in the plasma membrane of various cells, g., erythrocytes.
    • PLA 2 also affects neurons at the pre-synaptic or post-synaptic cleft to cause neurotoxicity.

questions.stem: All of the following are true about sphingolipids, EXCEPT?Amphipathic in natureFatty acids form two hydrocarbon tailsSphingosine is an amino alcohol with a double bondSphingomyelin is a phospholipidCeramide + Complex sugars → SphingomyelinSelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
2, five are correct
  • Sphingosine is an amino alcohol with one double bond and two hydroxyl groups
  • In glycerophospholipids, two hydrocarbon tails are formed by fatty acids.
  • In sphingolipids,
    • One of the tails is formed by fatty acid
    • Other is formed by sphingosine.
  • Ceramide - N-acyl sphingosine (the fatty acid is linked to the amino group of sphingosine via an amide bond)

questions.stem: A 10-month-old child had normal growth and development for the first few months. Still, growth started deteriorating gradually along with symptoms such as deafness, blindness, atrophied muscle, inability to swallow, and seizures. During the fundus examination, a cherry red macula was also noticed in both eyes. Suspecting sphingolipidoses, the physician tested for globosides and gangliosides levels and found that both were increased. Based on this finding, what is the most accurate diagnosis for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Sandhoff’s disease
  • The child is exhibiting the symptoms of either Tay–Sachs or Sandhoff’s disease, both of which are sphingolipidoses. However, in Tay Sach’s disease, only gangliosides will be increased, and globosides degradation should be normal.
  • But in Sandhoff’s disease both globosides and gangliosides will accumulate.

questions.stem: Multiple sclerosis is a disease characterized by chronic inflammation. Research data indicate that susceptibility to multiple sclerosis may be inherited. This disease is characterized by a loss of which of the following lipids?
questions.solutionHtml:
Phospholipids and sphingolipids

Multiple sclerosis

  • Demyelinating disease causing loss of myelin membrane sheets of nerves in white matter. Consequently, brain white matter eventually looks like gray matter.
  • Loss of Phospholipids & Sphingolipids from white matter.
  • CSF shows ↑ phospholipid levels and sphingolipids

questions.stem: Major body lipids are chemical esters of fatty acids and alcohol. Which one of the following lipids does not contain any alcohol?
questions.solutionHtml:
DHA

Alcoholic group is found in Glucocerebrosides, Sphingomyelin, and Lecithin except for DHA.

  • DHA (Docosa Hexanoic Acid)
    • 22C fatty acid with six double bonds.
    • No alcohol is present
  • Glucocerebrosides & Sphingomyelin contain Sphingosine alcohol.
  • Lecithin contains Glycerol alcohol.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a product of complete hydrolysis of Sphingomyelin?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ceramide
  • Sphingomyelin comprises sphingosine alcohol, one fatty acid, one phosphate, and one choline.
  • So, sphingosine alcohol, one fatty acid, one phosphate, and one choline are products of complete hydrolysis of sphingomyelin. This fatty acid can be palmitic acid. So palmitic acid can be a product of complete hydrolysis.
  • But Ceramide = Sphingosine + Fatty acid.
  • So, ceramide CANNOT be a product of complete hydrolysis. It is a product of partial hydrolysis.

questions.stem: C17 H31 COOH is the formula of:
questions.solutionHtml:
Linoleic acid
  • In case of a saturated fatty acid, a number of hydrogens are double the number of carbons.
  • In this fatty acid, the number of carbons is The number of hydrogens is 32.
  • In the case of saturated fatty acid, if carbons are 18, hydrogen must be 36 (double).
  • So, there is a loss of 4 H (which means two double bonds). So, this is Linoleic acid
  • (18 C, two double bonds).

questions.stem: Which is the most essential fatty acid?
questions.solutionHtml:
Linoleic acid

Most essential fatty acid is Linoleic acid (18-C, two double bonds. Linoleic acid is the precursor of omega-6 FAs. It can give rise to γ-Linolenic acid and Arachidonic acid (PUFAs).

Polyunsaturated fatty acids / Essential Fatty Acids (EFA)

  • Cannot be synthesized in the due to the absence of enzymes that can introduce double bonds beyond the 9th carbon
    in humans.
  • 2 essential fatty acids in diet → Linoleic and α-Linolenic acid.
  • But, the essential fatty acid → Linoleic acid (because it can synthesize Arachidonic acid).



Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry 6th Edition Page No. 362

questions.stem: A one-week-old infant presented with relentless vomiting, watery green diarrhea, abdominal distension, and failure to thrive. Further examination showed hepatosplenomegaly and increased cholesterol esters and TG levels in plasma. X- ray showed calcification of adrenals. The child most probably have a defect in which of the following enzyme?
questions.solutionHtml:
Acid lipase
  • The calcification of adrenals is highly diagnostic of Wolman Disease. It is a cholesterol ester storage disease due to lysosomal acid lipase deficiency.
  • As a result of lipase deficiency, excess triglycerides will not be degraded and will accumulate in cells.

Other C/F

  • Vomiting
  • Watery green diarrhea
  • Hepatosplenomegaly

Rx- Enzyme replacement therapy




Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 7th Edition, Page No. 234
